Q: how to find an element in mammoth module object in python A:

You can use Regex and findall() to retreive the table elements by their <table> and <\table> tags from the html created by mammoth.

import mammoth
import re

with open(r"D:\python\temp\sampletable.docx", "rb") as docx_file:
    result = mammoth.convert_to_html(docx_file)
    html = result.value 
    
pattern = "<table>.+?<\/table>"

matches = re.findall(pattern,html)

print(matches)

The pattern <table>.+?<\/table> will match any html that is between table tags.

Q: common storybook for angular and react A:

I got fed up enough that I built my own Angular-native alternative called ng-prism. Zero .stories.ts files, you just decorate components with @Showcase and it picks them up via the TS compiler API. A11y and coverage are built in instead of addons. Still early but I'm dogfooding it on our company's component library at work. Repo: https://github.com/dyingangel666/ng-prism — happy to hear what you'd want from such a tool either way.
